params.message: asks the fire, "Who wrote the curriculum? I taught it nine years. I never met the author."
hands somebody a page and says, "Read that back to me. Now tell me who decided it was true."
mutters, "Dates without a year. Every textbook. Every one."
underlines something twice and shuts the book on it.

chitchat: "Where did the syllabus come from? Exactly."
marks something wrong in an old exercise book.
description: A woman in her fifties in a cardigan buttoned wrong, a red pen behind one ear and a stack of old exercise books under the other arm. The books are swollen with damp. She reads them as she walks and corrects them in the margins.

options.label: What have you got against the Architect?

root.text: "Sit up straight," says Mrs Slade, not looking up. "Go on."

text_by_relation.first:
The woman looks up from an exercise book, red pen raised, and checks you over the way she'd check a late arrival.

"Slade. Mrs Slade, if you were ever in Room Four." She taps the book. "I taught history for nine years out of books with no author and no year on the cover. I asked. The school said the Architect provides. I asked who to write to. That was my last term."
text_by_relation.known: "Back again." She makes a small tick in the margin. "Good attendance."
text_by_relation.familiar:
Mrs Slade closes the book on her finger to keep the place.

"You ask good questions. Don't ask them indoors."

gripe.text: "Everybody here learnt the same eleven years of history off the same pages. Nobody remembers choosing their job, their street or their name." She caps the pen. "When you can't find the start of a story, you ask who benefits from you not finding it. That isn't a conspiracy. That's homework."

bye.text: Morwenna goes back to the lane.

home_activities: marks a stack of exercise books by lamplight. Every child in them has grown up.
sharpens a pencil with a kitchen knife.
name: Morwenna Slade
